properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-13, and this is the half of the template idea with a live user behind it rather than a hypothetical one.

TWO THINGS HE SAID THAT POINT THE SAME WAY:
 · "if an organization has specific governance and/or design practices, they could make a seed-template for their organization"
 · and concretely, from his own use in hxm_program: a template "could provide all the appropriate or approved references for the design to use (for example, use NSLS-II ansible repo for deployment, and n2sndocs for networking instructions, etc)"

⭐ WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE DOMAIN TEMPLATE, and not just a smaller version of it: a domain template supplies SHAPE — the parts, seams and checks a field expects. This supplies POINTERS — the specific repositories, document sets and house rules a particular organisation has already blessed. The first is "how do people in this field design"; the second is "what is this organisation's answer already". One is educational, the other is administrative, and they could be built independently.

⭐ IT IS ALSO THE CASE WHERE THE STALENESS OBJECTION IS WEAKEST. An industry standard moves on its own schedule and nobody tells you; an organisation's approved deployment repo is a thing that organisation controls, can point at, and already knows the state of. The warrant problem does not disappear, but it has an owner who is reachable.

WHAT IT MIGHT MEAN IN THIS DESIGN'S OWN VOCABULARY, none of it settled:
 · the references as Artifacts with `documents` edges, registered but not authored here
 · or as external dependencies, since `external_dependency` already exists as a relation
 · or as DesignRules, if "use the NSLS-II ansible repo for deployment" is a rule whose breach should be reportable — which is the governance-proposal question, and its answer belongs to the organisation rather than to reflow2

🛑 THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE THIS WORSE THAN NOTHING: an approved-reference list that goes unmaintained is a set of links pointing at moved repositories and retired document sets, carried into every new design in the organisation, with the design asserting they are approved. The failure is the same class as a stale domain template but with a shorter fuse, because infrastructure repositories move more often than standards do.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether hxm_program actually wants this or whether @ajs is reasoning from it as an example. He has used reflow2 on that program and is describing what would have helped; nobody has asked the program.
properties.name: OPEN — should an ORGANISATION's template carry the approved references a design must design against — the NSLS-II ansible repo for deployment, n2sndocs for networking — rather than only a domain shape?
properties.rationale: Kept separate from the domain-template question because the two have different owners, different staleness profiles and could be built independently — and because this one has a real deployment behind it (hxm_program, NSLS-II) rather than a hypothetical domain. Recorded as a brainstorm; @ajs stated no preference and asked for nothing to be built.
